source.title: Characterizing signal propagation to close the performance gap in unnormalized ResNets
source.authors: Andrew Brock; Soham De; Samuel L. Smith

record.tranche_reason: Compares test accuracy with and without added regularization that includes dropout, but does not isolate dropout from stochastic depth.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet accuracy for regularized and unregularized ResNets. Its regularized condition adds both stochastic depth and dropout; cited findings about other methods are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: Table 2 tests V5's batch-size dependence using ImageNet ResNet-50s trained for the same 15 epochs with batch-specific learning rates. Table 1 measures a combined dropout and stochastic-depth intervention, which cannot establish dropout's separate effect under V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the regularization subsection, but omits the paper's central conclusion: carefully designed normalization-free residual networks achieve competitive ImageNet accuracy without activation normalization. The authors report that combined dropout and stochastic depth improves NF-ResNets and does not substantially improve BN-ResNets overall; they do not identify dropout's independent contribution.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet ResNet training with explicit regularization comparison; dropout is paired with stochastic depth, and the paper does not isolate dropout's effect.
record.method_sensitivity: Effect differs between unnormalized and batch-normalized ResNets; the paper also reports training collapse for some unregularized 288-layer runs.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding stochastic depth and dropout together raises NF-ResNet accuracy by 1.0–1.7 percentage points. BN-ResNet changes range from −0.4 to +0.7 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of this combined regularization intervention depends on whether ResNets use batch normalization.

record.problems: The intervention combines dropout and stochastic depth, so the independent dropout contribution cannot be determined. The reported outcomes are ImageNet test accuracy, not an explicit train-test error gap. At depth 288, unregularized results are based on 3 successful seeds after two runs collapsed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
A batch-size sweep establishing a large-batch degradation threshold; longer-training remedies; language models. Table 2 compares batches 4, 8 and 1024 with different learning rates.
Dropout's separate effect, small-training-set effects, excessive-dropout underfitting, and removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

missing.what: NF-ResNet-50 batch comparison: ImageNet accuracy 69.9 ± 0.1%, 69.6 ± 0.1%, and 69.9 ± 0.1% at batches 1024, 8, and 4 respectively; all trained for 15 epochs, with learning rates 0.4, 0.025, and 0.01, without dropout or stochastic depth.

BN-ResNet-50 batch comparison under the same epoch budgets and batch-specific learning rates: 70.9 ± 0.1%, 65.7 ± 0.2%, and 55.7 ± 0.3% at batches 1024, 8, and 4 respectively. Results are medians and standard deviations across five seeds.

record.verdict_notes: Missing training accuracy does not prevent evaluating V6's held-out-error outcome; the obstacle is the combined intervention. Table 2 qualifies batch-size effects but does not establish that batch 1024 exceeds a workload-dependent large-batch threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large versus small batches under a fixed epoch budget.
Dropout is combined with stochastic depth; effects on very small training sets and under excessive dropout are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

relationships.condition: NF-ResNet-50 on ImageNet, 15 epochs, batch-specific learning rates
relationships.reason: From Table 2 text, missing from the rows: batch 1024 reaches 69.9%, versus 69.6% at batch 8 and 69.9% at batch 4, showing no larger-batch penalty in this tested recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy at batch 1024 was similar to or slightly better than with microbatches, small groups of examples processed separately. These comparisons remain unverified.
